hero.lead: A nation of 8.6 million building West Africa’s logistics hub, which signed $429 million with the World Bank in 2026, including $200 million to modernise its transport.

stats.label: Transport and logistics programme, all financiers

capital.heading: A port nation, financed as a hub.

record.text: Transport Connectivity and Logistics Improvement Program (PASLT), IDA, approved 16 June 2026
Total cost of the transport programme: World Bank $200 million, EIB $90 million, AIIB $75 million (approved 4 September 2026), private sector $20 million
Five financing agreements signed with the World Bank Group, reported 21 July 2026; active portfolio of $2.1 billion
IMF Extended Credit Facility, 42 months, approved March 2024; SDR 220.2 million (about US$298.63 million) disbursed by 29 June 2026
Total public debt, share of GDP, end-2025, down from a peak of 66.2% in 2024; moderate risk of overall and external debt distress

register.name: Five-year Treasury bond on the regional market (UMOA-Titres)
register.detail: State of Togo · OAT TG0000003557 · value date 27 July 2026 · coupon 6.35% · matures 27 July 2031
register.note: Amount outstanding at 31 October 2026, on the UMOA-Titres list of securities issued by auction
register.text: A five-year bond of the Public Treasury of Togo, sold by auction on the regional market of the West African Monetary Union, run by UMOA-Titres. In June 2026 the Treasury also issued three-, five- and seven-year bonds at coupons of 6.15% to 6.50%. It is borrowing in CFA francs, on the regional market.

register.name: Togo Digital Acceleration Project
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Approved 30 September 2026 · P179138
register.note: Principal as listed on the World Bank Group’s Finances One page for Togo
register.text: World Bank financing for the Togo Digital Acceleration Project, approved on 30 September 2026 with a principal of US$20 million. Digital networks and services carry payments, schooling and health care, and serve the livelihood, education and health standards.

register.name: Transport Connectivity and Logistics Improvement Project
register.detail: AIIB · Approved 4 September 2026 · sovereign-backed · P001063 · co-financing with the World Bank
register.note: Part of a $385 million programme: World Bank $200 million, EIB $90 million, private sector $20 million
register.text: Co-finances the World Bank’s transport and logistics programme: safe, climate-resilient connectivity to regions with high agricultural potential, and more efficient logistics and safer urban mobility in Greater Lomé. It serves food and livelihood, by linking farms to markets.

register.name: West Africa Unique Identification for Regional Integration and Inclusion (WURI), Phase 2
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Approved 30 June 2026 · P169594 · regional programme
register.note: Principal for Togo as listed on the World Bank Group’s Finances One page for Togo
register.text: Financing for Togo under the second phase of the regional programme for foundational identification in West Africa. A unique identity lets every resident be counted and reached by social protection, health care and financial services, across the seven standards.

register.name: Extended Credit Facility
register.detail: IMF · Approved 1 March 2024 · 42 months · SDR 293.6 million, 200% of quota · combined third and fourth reviews completed 29 June 2026
register.note: SDR 80.74 million (about US$109.5 million) released on 29 June 2026; SDR 220.2 million (about US$298.63 million) disbursed in all
register.text: The IMF’s lending programme with Togo, supporting fiscal consolidation, domestic revenue, the soundness of banks and the governance of the electricity sector. In June 2026 the Board granted waivers on three performance criteria and judged a temporary widening of the 2026 deficit appropriate to support vulnerable groups after the fuel price shock.

register.name: Power Regional Integration through Market-Enabled Gas Project (PRIME-GAS)
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Approved, release dated 29 June 2026 · with Benin and Côte d’Ivoire · $140 million in all
register.note: Togo’s share of $140 million; $55 million to Côte d’Ivoire and $45 million to Benin
register.text: Helps Benin, Côte d’Ivoire and Togo build national gas markets: coordinated gas imports, Gas Master Plans, harmonised regulation and the infrastructure to supply power plants and industry with more affordable and reliable natural gas. The World Bank expects it to unlock an estimated $1.5 billion in private investment; it serves energy.

register.name: Gulf of Guinea Northern Regions Social Cohesion Project (COSO), additional financing
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Approved 25 June 2026 · P175043 · third additional financing · with Benin and Côte d’Ivoire
register.note: Togo’s share of $163 million: a credit of EUR 52.5 million (US$61.5 million) and a grant of SDR 5.5 million (US$7.5 million)
register.text: Community investments, infrastructure, livelihood support and inclusion in the fragile northern border regions of Benin, Côte d’Ivoire and Togo. In Togo, 1,461 subprojects have already improved access to services for more than 500,000 people, including over 24,000 refugees; it serves livelihood and basic services.

register.name: Regional Access Increase and Sustainable Energy Project (RAISE)
register.detail: World Bank Group (IDA) · Approved 24 June 2026 · with ECOWAS · West Africa Regional Electricity Market Program
register.note: $160 million for Togo and The Gambia together; the share of Togo is not stated
register.text: Expands and densifies electricity distribution networks, lowers the cost of connection and speeds up renewable energy in Togo and The Gambia, with about 1 million people to be connected across the two. The World Bank expects labour income gains equal to about 9,200 jobs a year in Togo; it serves energy.

register.name: Transport Connectivity and Logistics Improvement Program (PASLT)
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Approved 16 June 2026 · P508939 · co-financed by the AIIB, the EIB and private capital
register.note: Some 2.2 million inhabitants, and about 400,000 rural people, 51% of them women, to benefit
register.text: Rehabilitates the railway between the Autonomous Port of Lomé and the Adetikopé Industrial Platform, improves urban mobility in Greater Lomé and rehabilitates feeder roads linking farms to markets in the Kara, Savanes, Plateaux and Plaine de Mô regions. It serves food and livelihood.

register.name: Private investment and job creation operation, first of a series
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Approved 12 December 2025 · first in a three-year programmatic series · about FCFA 84 billion
register.note: Expected to improve the employment conditions of 73,000 people over five years
register.text: Supports reforms for land security and finance for smallholder farmers, fewer constraints in energy, digital and logistics, stronger legal protection for foreign direct investment and better links between general and technical education. The World Bank says it could mobilise up to $800 million in additional private capital; it serves food and livelihood.

register.name: Second Development Policy Operation for sustainable, inclusive and resilient development
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Approved 10 December 2024 · P181238
register.note: The second operation of its series
register.text: Supports reforms for land tenure security for smallholders, a new electricity tariff structure and renewable generation, a framework for carbon credit markets, a national social registry, textbooks and teacher performance, and support for victims of gender-based violence. It touches food, energy, education and livelihood.

register.name: Sustainable Agricultural Transformation Program (ProMAT, phase 1)
register.detail: World Bank and IFC · Approved 11 June 2025 · First phase of the Agricultural Modernization Program 2025–2034
register.text: Makes Togo a regional hub for agribusiness and animal feed, led jointly by the World Bank and IFC.

register.name: Support Programme for Agricultural Mechanization and Irrigation (ProMAI), Phase II
register.detail: BOAD · Approved at the 151st Board meeting · release of 26 June 2026, Lomé · borrower: Republic of Togo
register.note: One of 11 operations of XOF 344.577 billion approved at the meeting
register.text: Finances modern agricultural mechanization and irrigation equipment, to raise agricultural productivity and producers’ incomes and strengthen food security. It serves food, where 56.3% of Togolese are moderately or severely food insecure, and livelihood.

register.name: Programme de Modernisation de l’Agriculture Togolaise (ProMAT), sovereign-backed facility
register.detail: Africa Finance Corporation · Lomé, 23 June 2026 · 10-year tenor · AFC Co-Mandated Lead Arranger and joint financier
register.note: Arranged for the Government of the Republic of Togo
register.text: Finances the purchase, assembly and distribution of agricultural machinery and equipment, including 2,126 tractor and trailer sets, 1,020 units of seeding and harvesting equipment, 930 irrigation units and 95 water supply systems. It serves food and livelihood.

register.name: Transit Roads and Transport Facilitation Project, phase 1 (CU18 corridor)
register.detail: African Development Fund · Loan approved 21 May 2026 · $59.78 million in all, with Benin · co-financed by the IsDB, WAEMU and the two governments
register.note: Togo’s section of the corridor; the Beninese section receives $9.5 million
register.text: Rehabilitates 78.8 kilometres of road between Kara and Kabou along the Benin-Togo border. Road users, particularly women, local producers and residents, are the expected beneficiaries; it serves livelihood and access to markets.

register.name: Label d’Or shea processing
register.detail: BOAD · Approved at the 150th Board session, Dakar, 25 and 26 March 2026
register.text: Modernises shea processing at Label d’Or, which buys from 33,000 women.

register.name: Gozem vehicle financing platform, expansion loans
register.detail: IFC · Approved 24 June 2026 · signed 26 June 2026 · Benin, Cameroon, Republic of Congo and Togo · 2026 to 2028
register.note: An IFC A loan of up to €8 million and a subordinated loan of up to €8 million (IDA21 Private Sector Window) for four nations; the share of Togo is not stated
register.text: Loans to expand the vehicle financing arm of Gozem, a super-app for ride-hailing, delivery, vehicle financing and mobile money. Vehicle financing helps drivers own the motorcycles and cars they work with; it serves livelihood.

register.name: Africa Lease Togo, loan for small businesses
register.detail: IFC · MSME Finance Platform · approved 30 June 2025 · committed 26 November 2025 · unsecured senior loan, up to 5 years, in euro
register.note: IFC’s own share of a loan of up to $30 million; the rest from other lenders
register.text: A loan to the largest leasing company in Togo, a new IFC client, to expand finance for small and medium enterprises, with at least 25% expected to be on-lent to agricultural SMEs. It serves livelihood and food.

register.name: Star Garments Group, Togo cut-make-trim expansion
register.detail: IFC · Approved 20 December 2023 · signed 29 March 2024 · Plateforme Industrielle d’Adétikopé, about 22 km from Lomé
register.note: IFC A loan of $7.5 million in a $15 million package, with a $7.5 million subordinated loan from the IDA Private Sector Window
register.text: Finances a new garment factory in the Adétikopé Industrial Platform, run by a new subsidiary of Star Garments Group. The project will create 2,000 new jobs; it serves livelihood.

register.name: Togocom network modernisation and expansion (Axian Togo)
register.detail: IFC · Approved 6 August 2021 · committed 8 February 2024 · loans from IFC’s own account and mobilised lenders
register.note: Up to $50 million from IFC’s own account and up to $72 million in mobilisation, as described; $59.51 million committed
register.text: Loans to Togocom, the mobile operator, to modernise and expand its network. Mobile networks carry the mobile money and digital services that families use for payments, schooling and health care; it serves livelihood.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Port
items.label: Greater Lomé residents served by the transport programme
items.text: A deep-water port and corridors to the Sahel: a hub that can be priced as an asset.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: Seven tenths of the land in agriculture, linked to the port by new corridors.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 40.4% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Aquaponie du Togo
items.text: Raises fish and vegetables together in a closed loop in Lomé, with water savings estimated at 90% compared with conventional agriculture, and designs kits and trains others in the technology. Its first system has run on a 40-square-metre site since November 2023, and demand has exceeded production.

items.name: Bboxx
items.text: Installs solar home systems and has operated in Togo since 2017; in 2019 its customers became the first in Africa to receive a government subsidy for solar energy payments, under the national CIZO electrification strategy. Over 100,000 Togolese people have access to clean energy at home, in their communities and in their businesses.

items.name: DokitaEyes
items.text: A digital health record launched in 2015: each patient’s medical record is reached through a QR code, with appointments, prescriptions, payments and test results. It has 45,000 users and more than 230 partner health facilities, and its monitoring programme supported nearly 15,000 pregnant women and nearly 70,000 children under five.

items.name: Gozem
items.text: A ride-hailing and delivery app whose V+ programme has helped 1,000 drivers become owners of motorcycles, cars and tricycles, repaid through daily payments over two years for motorcycles and four years for cars. IFC funding is to help 6,000 motorcycle taxi drivers in Togo and Benin acquire new vehicles.

items.name: WAGES
items.text: One of the leading microfinance institutions in Togo, offering credit and savings products to more than 15,000 borrowers and over 90,000 savers; 53% of its 131,178 beneficiaries are women.

items.name: Assilassimé
items.text: A microfinance institution that requires neither collateral nor guarantees, with low entry thresholds and training in managing an economic activity; women represent 90% of its 75,627 beneficiaries. About 30% of its beneficiaries have access to quality health care through a health mutual fund set up in 2023.
